review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the downstream test file SimplicialObjectsTest/PointHomology.lean, which uses the `_hom`/`_inv` simp lemmas and the comparison laws. I did not run Lean, so the stuck-simp behaviour below comes from reading the simp lemma shapes, not from an observed failure. The `_hom`/`_inv` simp lemmas are rfl projection lemmas and look fine. I did not recommend simp on `_class` or `_up`, because their left-hand sides are large and awkward. The same concern about missing `reassoc` applies to the two naturality theorems, but I left it out as less certain.

findings.problem: The file marks `tensorNormalizedHomologyZeroIsoCoefficient_hom` and `_inv` as simp. These rewrite `iso.hom` and `iso.inv` to the raw comparison morphisms `ToCoefficient` and `CoefficientToHomologyZero`. Simp rewrites subterms first, so a term `iso.hom ≫ iso.inv` becomes `ToCoefficient ≫ CoefficientToHomologyZero` before the generic `Iso.hom_inv_id` can apply. The only lemmas that cancel that composite are the two `_comp_` laws, and they are neither `@[simp]` nor `@[reassoc]`. The simp set therefore pushes iso compositions into a form it cannot close, and the `_assoc` form `f ≫ ToCoefficient ≫ FromCoefficient ≫ g` has no lemma at all. The downstream test works around this: it takes `.inv_hom_id`, runs `simp only [_inv, _hom] at h`, and then uses `rw [← Category.assoc, h, Category.id_comp]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` to both `_comp_` theorems. Then `ToCoefficient ≫ FromCoefficient = 𝟙` and its `_assoc` variant fire after the `_hom`/`_inv` lemmas have expanded the iso projections. Alternatively, drop `@[simp]` from `_hom`/`_inv` so `Iso.hom_inv_id` and `Iso.inv_hom_id` stay the canonical simplifiers. In either case, use `@[reassoc]` on the two laws so rewriting under a longer composite works.
findings.benefit: Simp then closes `φ ≫ β` and `β ≫ φ` compositions, including ones inside longer composites, with no manual `simp only ... at h` and `← Category.assoc` rewriting. This removes the competition between the iso projection lemmas and `Iso.hom_inv_id`, and keeps the simp normal form (the explicit morphisms) consistent.
